_doc: Outcome restrictions (harness/outcome_restriction.py): an UNRESTRICTED outcome never pools a row restricted by attribution or cause; the markers are verbatim phrasings of the restriction.

Adverse events leading to discontinuatio.definition: any adverse event leading to discontinuation of the trial regimen, whatever its attribution or cause

examples_refused.FOURIER: Thought to be related to the study agent and leading to discontinuation of study regimen | 226 (1.6) | 201 (1.5)
examples_refused.ODYSSEY OUTCOMES: Injection-site reactions (itching, redness, or swelling) were usually mild and self- limited and led to discontinuation of the trial regimen in 26 patients in the alirocumab group, at a median of 8.3 months after randomization, and in 3 patients in the placebo group.

Hypotension.definition: each row carries its own definition: symptomatic (clinical), reported-AE-with-SBP-threshold, symptomatic-with-SBP-threshold

NCT02554890.definition: Examine the effect of LCZ696 vs. enalapril on incidence of symptomatic hypotension during 8 weeks of treatment

witness.span: Examine the effect of LCZ696 vs. enalapril on incidence of symptomatic hypotension during 8 weeks of treatment

Hyperkalemia.definition: laboratory potassium thresholds (>5.5 vs >=5.5 mmol/L) are kept apart from CODED hyperkalaemia adverse events

NCT02554890.definition: Hyperkalemia is defined as Potassium level \>5.5 mEq/L.

witness.span: Hyperkalemia is defined as Potassium level \>5.5 mEq/L.

Diabetic ketoacidosis.definition: adjudicated DIABETIC ketoacidosis vs any ketoacidosis (EMPA-KIDNEY counts one in a participant without diabetes)

36331190.definition: ketoacidosis, adjudicated, Includes one event of ketoacidosis in a participant without diabetes at baseline

witness.span: Includes one event of ketoacidosis in a participant without diabetes at baseline

Hyperkalemia.definition: serious / investigator-reported / laboratory-threshold hyperkalaemia are DIFFERENT definitions; a pool never spans them

witness.span: The incidence of serious hyperkalemia was minimal in both groups of patients.
A serum potassium level exceeding 5.5 mmol per liter occurred in 11.8% of patients in the eplerenone group and 7.2% of those in the placebo group (P<0.001).
